title: dedicated: improve fleet autoscaler burst controls and utilization reporting (v3)
author: Evan Brooks
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally see short-lived demand spikes which cause transient latency SLO violations and unexpected cost due to overprovisioning. This PR tightens burst controls on the fleet autoscaler and improves utilization reporting so operators can understand burst consumption and make better capacity commitments. Changes: 1) Introduced a new burst_budget controller on the fleet autoscaler that tracks per-fleet burst credits and enforces a sliding window spend rate. 2) Added an explicit throughput_guarantee config per fleet allowing operators to pin a minimum token/s throughput and expose the residual as burstable capacity. 3) Enhanced utilization reporting: the monitor now emits burst_consumed, burst_remaining, and guaranteed_throughput metrics with labels for fleet_id, model_family, and region. 4) Safety: added fallback policies that automatically route to lower-cost model variants when burst budget is exhausted and latency SLO would be violated. 5) Docs and console: updated dedicated/autoscaling.md and console dashboards to show burst budget and historical burn-down. Testing and rollout: unit and integration tests added for budget accounting and fallback routing. We ran a canary across three small fleets for 48 hours with synthetic spike traffic; results show 35% fewer SLO violations and 18% lower peak provisioning compared to v2. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (Linear ENG-2189) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests (local k8s harness) - [x] E2E canary results attached - [x] Docs updated - [x] Console dashboard updated Backwards compatibility: existing fleet configs are compatible; if throughput_guarantee is unset the autoscaler behaves as before. Rollout plan: staged canary followed by gradual rollout to remaining fleets over two weeks. Related: follows up on prior autoscaler work in ENG-1740 and addresses operational fallout described in incident INT-5221.

review_comments: Aisha Patel: Can you clarify how burst credits are serialized across restarts? Suggest persisting to the fleet CR status field and reconciling on startup.
Evan Brooks: We persist credits to the fleet status in burst_budget.go; added reconciliation logic and unit tests. See commit ef8b3a1.
Marcus Liang: The fallback routing could cause quality regressions for some workloads. Please add a feature flag and a gradual rollout option in the API.
Evan Brooks: Added a 'fallback_enabled' flag on the fleet spec; default is true for canary and can be turned off per customer. Also added an operator-level rollout control.
Sofia Gomez: CI flakes on metrics schema job; can we add schema validation and a retry? Also include a migration step for existing dashboards.

Aisha Patel: Approve after addressing persistence and rollout controls.

release_notes: Improved fleet autoscaler with burst budgeting, throughput guarantees, enhanced utilization metrics, and safer fallback routing. Operators can now set throughput_guarantee per fleet and monitor burst_consumed/remaining to make more accurate capacity commitments.
